blocker_1_new_bypass_case_sensitive_nume.payload: [x](javascript:alert(1))  -- note uppercase X in the hex marker, valid per HTML5's numeric-character-reference grammar (the x/X marker is explicitly case-insensitive; s and s are the same reference)
blocker_1_new_bypass_case_sensitive_nume.reproduced: Letflow.Help.HelpContent.create_changeset/2 on this body: valid? == true, errors == [] -- the javascript: payload is accepted and would be written live to help_content.body untouched.
blocker_1_new_bypass_case_sensitive_nume.code_path_reason: lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex:127's @numeric_entity_pattern is `~r/&#(x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+);/` -- the hex-form alternative hardcodes a literal lowercase `x`, with no `/i` flag and no `[xX]` alternative, even though decode_entity_code/1 (line 280) is itself written to accept both (`x in [?x, ?X]`) -- the capturing regex never gets the chance to hand it an uppercase form. Because decode_numeric_entities/1 fails to match `s` at all, the entity survives un-decoded into scheme_letters/1 (line 262), which downcases the whole pre-colon span (`"javascript"` -> `"javascript"`) BEFORE filtering to ASCII a-z -- the now-lowercased literal `x` marker character from the un-decoded entity syntax itself survives the a-z filter as a real letter, producing the extracted scheme `"javaxcript"` (extra `x` injected) instead of `"javascript"`. `"javaxcript"` is not in @disallowed_url_schemes, so unsafe_scheme?/1 returns false.
blocker_1_new_bypass_case_sensitive_nume.why_this_is_the_same_bug_class_the_last_: Same root cause REVIEWER's determination (step-03d) already named: a check written against an assumed-normalized string, defeated by an encoding variant the check's own author didn't enumerate -- previously CommonMark-syntax variants (reference-style, angle-bracket), now an HTML5-entity-syntax variant (hex marker case).

blocker_2_new_bypass_raw_tag_split_acros.reproduced: Both: Letflow.Help.HelpContent.create_changeset/2 -- valid? == true, errors == []. Confirmed via EarmarkParser.as_ast/2 directly first: `[{"p", [], ["xy"], %{}}]` -- three children, and the raw tag's own '<' and '>' each live in a DIFFERENT string sibling.
blocker_2_new_bypass_raw_tag_split_acros.code_path_reason:
lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex:219's fallback `walk(text) when is_binary(text)` scans each plain-text AST leaf independently against @raw_html_tag_pattern (`~r/<\/?[a-zA-Z][^<>]*>/`, requires both a literal '<' and a literal '>' within the SAME leaf). walk/1's list clause (line 198) calls this per-child, never reassembling sibling text nodes before scanning. Any inline construct that interrupts the raw tag's own attribute area -- `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, and by the same mechanism emphasis/links/anything earmark treats as its own inline node -- splits the leading `` fragment into separate list elements, and neither fragment alone contains a complete `<...>` span, so neither leaf matches. Contrast with the one payload that appeared similar but is NOT a bypass (`x
y
` -- caught): that one happens to still carry a separate, complete `` closing tag intact in its own trailing leaf, which independently matches the pattern. The bypass is real whenever the payload has no such redundant complete tag elsewhere.
blocker_2_new_bypass_raw_tag_split_acros.severity_note: This defeats the exact mechanism blocker_1 of ELIXIR-DEV's own rework2 summary calls out as the fix for gap 1 (inline-mixed raw HTML) -- the fallback scan closes the case where earmark declines to produce a verbatim node, but only when the raw tag's angle brackets survive in one unbroken text run; it was never checked against the case where earmark's own inline-node splitting breaks that assumption, which is the ordinary case for any raw tag that happens to contain markdown-significant characters in its attribute value.

payloads_no_attack_intent_required: some text with `unclosed code   (a single stray unmatched backtick)
blocker_3_inv8_bare_match_crashes_on_rea.reproduced: Both raise `** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, ast, [...]}` at lib/letflow/help/help_content.ex:178, inside the anonymous fn passed to Ecto.Changeset.validate_change/3 -- propagates straight out of create_changeset/2 (and equally update_changeset/2), i.e. out of Letflow.Help.create_draft/2 and update_draft/3, uncaught.
blocker_3_inv8_bare_match_crashes_on_rea.code_path_reason: help_content.ex:178 is `{:ok, ast, _messages} = EarmarkParser.as_ast(value)`, a bare 3-tuple match assuming the :ok branch always fires. EarmarkParser.as_ast/2's own documented contract (deps/earmark_parser/lib/earmark_parser.ex:15, `@type t :: {:ok, ast(), []} | {:error, ast(), errors()}`) and its own implementation (lines 623-631) set status to :error whenever ANY emitted message has severity :warning OR :error -- not only for a genuinely-unparseable document. Real trigger conditions confirmed live in this earmark_parser version: an unclosed inline backtick run (parser.ex:237 emits `:warning, "Closing unclosed backquotes"`), an unclosed fenced code block (parser.ex:505 emits `:error, "Fenced Code Block opened ... not closed"`), an undefined footnote reference (ast/inline.ex:444), and illegal inline attribute syntax (attr_parser.ex:67) all hit this path. None of these require adversarial intent -- a tenant author who simply forgets a closing backtick while writing ordinary help text crashes the write path.
blocker_3_inv8_bare_match_crashes_on_rea.invariant: INV-8 -- 'Error handling uses typed results ... for any path that touches external I/O, tenant-controlled data, or network input. A bare pattern match that can raise on realistic input ... is a defect.' `value` here is directly the tenant-authored `:title`/`:body` field content -- exactly the input class INV-8 names. This is not a supervised-process-restart case (no per-instance isolation here, per the invariant's own carve-out) -- it is a changeset validator called synchronously inside Letflow.Help's write path, so the crash surfaces directly to that call's caller.

non_security_finding_flagged_for_visibil.routing: Flagging for REVIEWER/ELIXIR-DEV rather than gating on it directly -- not a security invariant, but recorded here since it blocks the very test-run verification this round was also asked to perform, and per core-directives.md 'Never resolve a conflict/finding silently.'

required_fix: Route back to ELIXIR-DEV (third rework round on the implementation, not a fourth design round -- the AST-based mechanism itself remains sound; these are implementation-level gaps in how the mechanism's own edge cases and the library's documented status contract are handled): (1) make @numeric_entity_pattern's hex branch case-insensitive (`/i` flag or `[xX]`) so it matches decode_entity_code/1's own already-case-insensitive intent; (2) fix the plain-text fallback scan to detect a raw tag whose '<' and '>' land in different AST siblings -- e.g. reassemble/concatenate adjacent unstructured leaves (bounded to the same parent's children, still excluding code/pre content) before applying @raw_html_tag_pattern, rather than scanning each leaf in isolation; (3) replace the bare `{:ok, ast, _messages} = EarmarkParser.as_ast(value)` match with a `case`/`with` that treats EarmarkParser's own `{:error, ast, messages}` branch as a validation failure (add_error, same contract as every other rejection here) rather than letting it crash -- note the AST is still usable/present in the :error tuple, so this is not a loss of the walk's own results, just correct handling of the library's documented return contract; (4) separately, someone must add "help_content" to test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's @expected_tenant_tables so the test suite's claimed 47-pass result can actually be reproduced.
not_reopening: The AST-based mechanism itself (decision 0036, REVIEWER's option-b determination) is not in question -- these are implementation gaps within that mechanism, the same category of finding as rounds 1-2, not evidence the mechanism choice was wrong.
